chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Abdullah ibn Jabala from Ibn Bukayr from Ubayd ibn Zurara from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the woman whose husband dies, can she perform Hajj and testify for the rights? He said: Yes.

key_terms.الْحُقُوقَ: The rights (plural of haqq, referring to financial or legal dues owed by the husband)

ai.seo_question: Can a widow perform Hajj and testify for her husband's rights before her Iddah ends?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that a widow whose marriage was consummated retains the capacity to perform Hajj and testify for her husband's rights during her Iddah, dispelling potential confusion regarding her mobility and legal agency. It highlights the Shia juristic view that the waiting period primarily concerns residence and remarriage restrictions, rather than a suspension of all religious or legal duties. The chain of transmission underscores the reliability of the Kufan school of hadith in establishing these practical rulings.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Sama’at,f rom Abdullah Bin Jabala, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Ubeyd Bin Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
regarding the woman widowed from her husband, can she perform Hajj, or testify for the rights?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’.
en.sarwar: 3. Al-Husayn from Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali or others from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sulayman who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a widow if she can go out to the house of her father and mother from her house, if she so chooses, to complete her waiting period.

He (the Imam) said, ‘If she wants to complete her waiting period in the house of her husband, she can do so. If she wants to complete it in the house of her family she must not use kohl or wear ornaments.’ ”
